{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2022}} {{Use Indian English|date=June 2022}} {{Infobox port | name = Port of Pipavav | image = Berth portpipavav.JPG | image_caption = Ship docked at a container berth | logo = Port of pipavav logo.JPG | logo_size = 150px | country = India | location = [[Rajula]], Gujarat | coordinates = {{coord|20|55|8|N|71|30|15|E}} | locode = INPAV | opened = 2002 (Commercial operations) | operated = [[APM Terminals]] | owner = Gujarat Pipavav Port Limited (GPPL) | type = Deep water | berths = 4 container berths,
2 bulk berths,
1 liquid cargo jetty,
1 ro-ro jetty{{Cite web |url=https://shipnext.com/port/pipavav-inpav-ind |title=Pipavav Port Data and Shipping Insights |website=Shipnext |publisher=Shipnext BV |access-date=27 January 2026}} | draft_depth = {{convert|14.5|m|ft|abbr=on}} maximum }} '''Port Pipavav''' is a multi-user, multi-commodity, all weather port on the west coast of [[India]] in the Saurashtra region of [[Gujarat]], 90 km South of [[Amreli]], 15 km South of [[Rajula]] and 140 km Southwest of [[Bhavnagar]]. The port has cargo operations for [[Containerisation|containers]], [[Bulk cargo|bulk]], liquid and [[roll-on/roll-off]] cargo and an adjoining [[shipyard]] that builds naval vessels. == History == === Cargo port === In 1986 the Indian government authorized an expenditure of 5 million rupees to initiate port development near the village of [[Pipavav]] in the [[Amreli district]] of the state of Gujarat in India. The company GPPL was incorporated on 5 August 1992 to build, construct, operate and maintain the port. The company was initially a joint venture between [[Gujarat Maritime Board]] (GMB) and the SKIL Ports & Logistics division of the SKIL Infrastructure group (now known as Mercantile Ports and Logistics (MPL)).{{cite web |title=Gujarat Pipavav Port: Reports, Company History, Directors Report, Chairman's Speech, Auditors Report of Gujarat Pipavav Port |url=https://www.ndtv.com/business/stock/gujarat-pipavav-port-ltd_gppl/reports |date=2024-07-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509055415/https://www.ndtv.com/business/stock/gujarat-pipavav-port-ltd_gppl/reports |archive-date=2023-05-09 |url-status=dead}} In June 1998, GMB divested its stake in favour of SKIL Ports & Logistics. In 2000, GPPL formed a joint venture with [[Indian Railways]] to start Pipavav Rail Corporation Limited. Commercial operations started in 2002. The [[A.P. Moller-Maersk Group]] acquired a 13.5% equity interest in the company in June 2001. Pursuant to the share sale and purchase agreement dated 30 March 2005, SKIL Infrastructure, Nikhil Gandhi, Montana Valves and Compressors and Grevek Investment and Finance divested their shareholding in the company in favour of [[APM Terminals]]. === Shipyard === Construction of a shipyard adjoining the port was completed in 2010 by Pipavav Defence and Offshore Engineering Company Limited. In 2011 the shipyard won its first contract to build warships for the [[Indian Navy]].{{Cite report |title=Pipavav Defence and Offshore Engineering Company Limited – Annual Report 2010-11 |url=https://www.bseindia.com/bseplus/annualreport/533107/5331070311.pdf |date=September 2011 |publisher=Bombay Stock Exchange |access-date=17 July 2024}} The shipyard company was renamed to Reliance Defence and Engineering on 3 March 2016 and again renamed to Reliance Naval and Engineering Limited on 6 September 2017.{{Cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/reliance-defence-and-engineering-limited-is-renamed-r-navel/article19645496.ece|title=Reliance Defence and Engineering Limited is renamed R-NAVEL|date=8 September 2017 |newspaper=The Hindu |url-access=subscription |access-date=18 May 2018 |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} In January 2025 the company was renamed to [[Swan Defence and Heavy Industries Limited]].{{Cite news| url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/swan-defence-shares-re-list-on-stock-exchanges-up-5-after-listing/articleshow/117388734.cms |title=Swan Defence shares re-list on stock exchanges, up 5% after listing |last=Sharma |first= Riya |date=20 January 2025 |newspaper=The Economic Times |access-date=27 February 2025}} == Shialbet island == [[Koli people#Shial bet island|Shialbet island]] is a natural breakwater facing the wharves of the port. It is inhabited by a small fishing community and is connected to the mainland. {{Clear}} == Cargo operations == {{Infobox company | name = Gujarat Pipavav Port Limited | logo = | trade_name = APM Terminals Pipavav | type = Public | traded_as = {{BSE|533248}}
{{NSE|GPPL}} | founded = {{Start date and age|df=y|1992|08|05}} | founder = [[Gujarat Maritime Board]] (GMB) | hq_location = [[Rajula]], Gujarat | key_people = Keld Pedersen ([[Managing director|MD]])
Hariharan Iyer ([[CFO]])
Ravindranath Pillarisetti(Head-Port Infrastructure & Facility) | industry = [[Transport]], [[Port|Port Terminals]] | website = http://www.pipavav.com }} The cargo port is owned by the public company '''Gujarat Pipavav Port Limited''' (GPPL), and is operated by their majority owner APM Terminals, who are one of the largest [[container terminal]] operators in the world. Container, bulk, liquid, [[Liquefied petroleum gas|LPG]] an Roll-on/roll-off cargo can be handled. Services provided include pilotage/towage, cargo handling and logistics support.{{Cite web| url=https://www.apmterminals.com/en/pipavav/about/our-terminal |title=Our Port – APM Terminals |publisher=APM Terminals |access-date=17 July 2024}} === Port characteristics === The port is along major trade routes and is close to the major Indian port of [[Nhava Sheva]] (about 160 Nm). It has been dredged to allow a maximum draft of {{convert|14.5|m|ft}}. There are 8 quay [[Container crane|cranes for containers]], 2 mobile harbor cranes for handling bulk cargo, 4 rail mounted [[gantry cranes]] and 20 [[Rubber tyred gantry crane]]s. For [[refrigerated shipping]], the port is operated by a single entity i.e. it is a captive port.{{cite web |last=Punnathara |first=C.J. |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.in/bline/2010/04/29/stories/2010042951391800.htm |title=Gujarat makes giant strides in seafood exports |website=The Hindu Business Line |date=29 April 2010 |access-date=28 April 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120921025547/http://www.thehindubusinessline.in/bline/2010/04/29/stories/2010042951391800.htm |archive-date=21 September 2012}}{{Failed verification|date=March 2025}} == References == {{Reflist}} [[Category:2002 establishments in Gujarat]] [[Category:Infrastructure completed in 2002]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Gujarat]] [[Category:Ports and harbours of Gujarat]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]

The port has cargo operations for containers, bulk, liquid and roll-on/roll-off cargo and an adjoining shipyard that builds naval vessels.
